'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Battle of Donbas (2022)|Battle of Donbas]]
****[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] reportedly shell the administration headquarters of the [[Donetsk People's Republic]] in separatist-held [[Donetsk]], killing three people, according to pro-[[Russia]]n officials. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-strikes-administration-headquarters-donetsk-russia-installed-separatists-2022-08-23/ (Reuters)]
***[[List of military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|Foreign aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
****[[Slovakia]] announces that it will send an additional 30 [[BMP-1]] [[infantry fighting vehicle]]s and ammunition to [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/slovakia-donate-30-infantry-fighting-vehicles-ukraine-minister-2022-08-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Libyan Crisis (2011–present)|Libyan Crisis]]
**According to the [[Libyan National Army]], a United States-manufactured [[General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper|MQ-9 Reaper]] drone was shot down with a [[surface-to-air missile]], crashing near [[Benina International Airport]] in [[Benghazi]], [[Libya]]. [https://eurasiantimes.com/mq-9-reaper-drone-shot-down-near-benghazi-video/ (''Eurasian Times'')] [https://en.mehrnews.com/news/190589/US-General-Atomics-MQ9-Reaper-drone-shot-down-in-Libya (Mehr News Agency)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Holocene extinction]]
**The [[dugong]] is declared [[extinction|extinct]] in [[China]] after scientists report no verified sightings of the large [[marine mammal]] since 2000. However, dugongs still exist in the wild in parts of [[Southeast Asia]] and [[Australasia]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-62638485 (BBC News)]
*[[South Korea]] registers a population decrease for the second consecutive year, due to having [[List of sovereign states and dependencies by total fertility rate|the world's lowest birth rate]]. [https://english.news.cn/20220823/e8fa512b157045198f621ca51f58bcff/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal]]
**The [[Federal Court of Malaysia]] upholds the [[Corruption in Malaysia|corruption]] conviction and 12-year prison term of former [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|prime minister]] [[Najib Razak]] in connection with the [[embezzlement]] of [[sovereign wealth fund]]s from [[1Malaysia Development Berhad]]. Najib is the first former [[Malaysia]]n prime minister to be imprisoned. [https://www.npr.org/2022/08/23/1118960767/malaysia-top-court-upholds-ex-prime-minister-najibs-graft-conviction (NPR)]
*[[Gretchen Whitmer kidnapping plot]]
**Two men are found guilty of conspiring to obtain a weapon of mass destruction for use in the foiled plot to kidnap [[Michigan]] Governor [[Gretchen Whitmer]]. One of the men is also convicted of an explosives charge. [https://apnews.com/article/elections-presidential-michigan-gretchen-whitmer-grand-rapids-9ad8f100d32e7d5883b1be9d6c4cb8d5 (AP)]
*[[Brazilian police]] conduct eight raids on pro-Bolsonaro businessmen accused of discussing the possibility of a [[coup d'état]] if incumbent [[President of Brazil|President]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] loses the upcoming [[2022 Brazilian presidential election|presidential election]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-police-raid-pro-bolsonaro-businessmen-accused-coup-talk-sources-say-2022-08-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Scott Morrison ministerial positions controversy]]
**[[Australia]]n [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Anthony Albanese]] announces an official inquiry into his predecessor [[Scott Morrison]]'s secret swearing of himself into various ministerial positions during his [[Second Morrison ministry|second ministry]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2022/aug/23/anthony-albanese-scott-morrison-australia-politics-solicitor-general (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2022 Samoan o le Ao o le Malo election]]
**[[Tuimalealiʻifano Vaʻaletoʻa Sualauvi II]] is re-elected by the [[Parliament of Samoa|Parliament]] for a second term as [[O le Ao o le Malo]], the [[Samoa]]n head of state. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/473339/samoan-parliament-re-elects-head-of-state (RNZ)]
